title: EA Almanac — 2-5 Exploration & Agency
purpose: Parent-facing developmental reference; not a tracker or diagnostic tool.

entries.text: Language becomes a tool for thinking.
Adult roles are copied in pretend.
Preferences and identities become more visible.
Language is used to resist as well as request.
Concrete rules are easier to use.
Fantasy and reality can be explored together.
Children explain more of their reasoning.
Fatigue can make the child rigid.
Safety knowledge still needs adult protection.
Encourage new food exposure without pressure.
Avoid turning every rule into a negotiation.
Avoid fast distracting media as default.
Avoid media to stop every feeling.
Avoid assuming an educational app replaces interaction.
Avoid taking over simple tasks for speed.
Avoid public behavior as the whole score.
Avoid assuming swimming skill eliminates drowning risk.
Avoid assuming every safety rule will be remembered.
Avoid equating eye contact with respect.
Avoid forcing sharing of prized items.
Avoid solving every peer conflict immediately.
Avoid removing all boundaries in the name of independence.

They know more than they can consistently control.
Play is a primary learning environment.
Pretend play exercises thinking and social life.
The goal is competence, not compliance.
Let safe problems belong to the child.
Do not rescue a task because the child is slower.
Ask before telling when curiosity can teach.
Not every conversation needs a lesson.
Do not use shame to teach social behavior.
Repair need not be a performance of remorse.
Kindness does not require unwanted hugs.
Fair does not always mean identical.
Preschoolers can sense fairness before living it consistently.
Emotion words work best before crises.
Practice waiting while everyone is calm.
Real work can teach more than pretend work.
A tiny job can build competence.
Do not make food the battlefield.
New foods may need repeated low-pressure exposure.
Shared media is often more useful than solo use.
Outdoor play can be movement and science at once.
A walk can become science without becoming a lesson.
Museums work best when curiosity leads.
Do not turn every outing into a worksheet.
Rule changes are part of learning rules.
No can be the first form of autonomy.
Do not over-read defiance as disrespect.
Transitions can masquerade as discipline problems.
Water is not a place for unsupervised independence.
Children should not carry the whole hazard map in memory.
Apologize when you make a mistake.
Do not make them manage your emotions.
You do not have to stop every tear.
The parent is part of the environment.
Change the environment before judging character.
Sharing is not the only route to generosity.
Peer conflict can be practice when everyone is safe.
Step in for safety or power imbalance.
Boredom can need agency, not entertainment.
Do not fill every empty moment.
Normal variation is not a defect.
The Almanac is for noticing, not diagnosing.
The larger question is what matters about this stage that is easy to miss.
